name: Jehallelel
overview: Jehallelel was a male Levite belonging to the Merarite branch, descendants of Merari, son of Levi. He is specifically noted as the father of Azariah and lived during the reign of King Hezekiah. His role as a Merarite situates him within the Levitical priestly divisions responsible for the care of the tabernacle and temple services.
namesAndTitles: The name Jehallelel means 'he shall praise G-d [El]' or 'G-d [El] shines forth,' reflecting a theocentric meaning that honors God's presence and praise. This proper name is recorded in 2 Chronicles 29:12 and was not given directly by God but carries significant spiritual connotation.
familyAndRelationships: Jehallelel is identified as the father of Azariah, a relationship inferred from Scripture. He is also explicitly noted as a descendant of Merari, linking him to the Merarite clan within the tribe of Levi. Beyond these, Scripture does not provide additional family details.
scriptureSignificance: Jehallelel's significance lies in his position as a Merarite Levite during King Hezekiah's reign, a period marked by temple restoration and religious reform. As the father of Azariah, he connects to the priestly leadership involved in these reforms, underscoring the continuity of Levitical service. His mention in 2 Chronicles 29:12 highlights the importance of Levitical families in maintaining proper worship and temple duties under God's covenant.
